# One program through codespec

Generated by `codespec-docs` from the checked-in files of [`examples/greeter`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/tree/main/examples/greeter); `task examples` writes them and `task check` fails when any of them, or this page, drifts. The direction shown is the one that runs today: Go → `cir/1` → Rust, and Go → `cir/1` → Go.

:::note[In progress]

Rust → `cir/1` → Go needs the Rust reader, which is part of 0.1.0 and in progress ([Vision](/docs/vision#milestones)); this tree has no reader for Rust yet.

:::

## 1. The source

A small in-memory greeting service in Go. `cir/1` has no network I/O, so this is a service object rather than a server: a call such as `http.ListenAndServe` is read as a `foreign` statement ("expression outside cir/1") and the Rust writer refuses the function that holds it.

```go title="examples/greeter/source/greeter.go"
// Package greeter greets people by name and counts how often each was greeted.
package greeter

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

var ErrNoName = errors.New("name must not be empty")

type Greeter struct {
	greeted map[string]int
}

func New() *Greeter {
	return &Greeter{greeted: map[string]int{}}
}

func (g *Greeter) Greet(name string) (string, error) {
	if name == "" {
		return "", ErrNoName
	}
	g.greeted[name] = g.greeted[name] + 1
	return fmt.Sprintf("Hello, %s!", name), nil
}

func (g *Greeter) Count(name string) (int, bool) {
	n, ok := g.greeted[name]
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	return n, true
}
```

## 5. Write: `cir/1` → Rust

```shell-session
$ codespec write --lang rust examples/greeter/greeter.cir.json --out examples/greeter/out/rust --adapters target/adapters
```

The Rust writer (`codespec-write-rust`, on `syn` and `prettyplease`) reads its mappings off the facts: `Greet` is `fallible`, so it returns `Result<String, Error>`; `Count` is `comma_ok` and `read_only`, so it takes `&self` and returns `Option<i64>`; the sentinel error becomes a variant of one `Error` enum; Go's `int` is `i64` with wrapping arithmetic. It refused nothing:

```json title="examples/greeter/out/rust/refusals.json"
[]
```

```rust title="examples/greeter/out/rust/src/lib.rs"
// Code generated by codespec-write-rust from cir/1. DO NOT EDIT.
//! Package greeter greets people by name and counts how often each was greeted.
#![allow(dead_code, unused_assignments, unused_mut)]
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fmt;
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Greeter {
    greeted: BTreeMap<String, i64>,
}
pub fn new() -> Greeter {
    Greeter {
        greeted: BTreeMap::new(),
    }
}
impl Greeter {
    pub fn greet(&mut self, name: String) -> Result<String, Error> {
        if name == String::from("") {
            return Err(Error::ErrNoName);
        }
        self.greeted
            .insert(
                name.clone(),
                self.greeted.get(&name).cloned().unwrap_or(0i64).wrapping_add(1i64),
            );
        Ok(format!("Hello, {}!", name))
    }
    pub fn count(&self, name: String) -> Option<i64> {
        let Some(n) = self.greeted.get(&name).cloned() else {
            return None;
        };
        Some(n)
    }
}
/// Every error the module produces: its sentinel errors, its error types, and
/// `Msg` for a formatted message.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Error {
    ErrNoName,
}
impl fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Error::ErrNoName => f.pad("name must not be empty"),
        }
    }
}
impl std::error::Error for Error {}
```

## What this does not show

- The [harness](/docs/concepts/harness) compares implementations byte for byte on seeded traces. Its trace format is the `orders` service's, so `greeter` is checked by its build and by equality with the checked-in outputs, not by the harness.
- Writing `g.greeted[name]++` instead of `g.greeted[name] = g.greeted[name] + 1` is refused by the Rust writer today ("a write into a map entry's value"); the example uses the form it writes.
